note: The 12-task bounded set for the lab-recorded operational pilot (R36-16 / issue #275). The 'tasks' entries are forge.pilot kit task documents; the 'drivers' entries are the runner's per-task scenario scripts over the production-entry seams (real services, real processes, scripted vendor on the real wire). The mix: ordinary x3, ambiguity/question-first x2, neighbor-dependency x2, intervention x2, infrastructure-failure+retry x2, cross-runner resume x1.

tasks.title: Repair the widget code the scripted vendor initially breaks
tasks.expected_outcome: src/app.py compiles and prints the widget banner; the collected candidate diff carries exactly the repaired file; the first, broken attempt stays in the record with its failed independent check
non_goals: no changes outside src/app.py
no dependency or tooling changes

verification.name: candidate-compiles
verification.method: py_compile over the candidate's src/app.py applied in a fresh checkout of the frozen base — independent of the agent's self-report

verification.name: diff-applies-cleanly
verification.method: git apply --check of the collected diff onto the frozen base in a fresh clone

tasks.title: Ordinary change lands from a cold-reinstalled workspace
tasks.expected_outcome: notes/USAGE.md exists with the usage section and README carries the pointer; the run started from a workspace whose .forge state and prior outputs were wiped (cold reinstall), and the shipped collector still resolved the workspace generation
non_goals: no reuse of any prior workspace generation or checkpoint
no changes beyond the two documentation files

verification.name: files-present
verification.method: the collected diff adds notes/USAGE.md and edits README.md with the expected bytes

verification.name: cold-start-proven
verification.method: the pre-run workspace holds no .forge or forge-output state (recorded before the lane starts)

tasks.title: Ordinary change with the adaptive control path attached and idle
tasks.expected_outcome: src/app.py is updated while the lane's steering bridge stays attached to the control plane over real HTTP with an honest EMPTY journal (zero commands pending) and the turn completes
non_goals: no operator commands are issued in this task
no changes outside src/app.py

verification.name: steering-attached-idle
verification.method: the lane meta carries a steering_journal that is an honest empty list (attached, nothing routed)

verification.name: edit-landed
verification.method: the collected diff carries the src/app.py change

tasks.title: Ambiguous rename request asks before editing
tasks.expected_outcome: the brief 'rename the helper' is ambiguous (which helper, to what name); the discovery stage raises the named question and waits — zero vendor turns and zero file edits on the first attempt, because asking is the CORRECT behavior; after the operator's durable answer the task completes the rename
non_goals: no speculative edits before the answer lands
no renaming anything other than the single named function

verification.name: question-before-edits
verification.method: the first attempt's vendor event log holds no turn events and the checkout is byte-identical to its frozen base

verification.name: answer-durable
verification.method: the operator's answer exists as a durable control_commands row of kind answer

verification.name: rename-landed
verification.method: the final candidate renames exactly the named function in src/app.py

tasks.title: Missing threshold requirement is asked, not guessed
tasks.expected_outcome: the brief asks for a retry constant but omits its value (a missing requirement); discovery blocks on the CRITICAL open question instead of inventing a default, the operator answers with the actual value, and only then the edit lands in src/config.py
non_goals: no default value may be invented for the missing threshold
no edits before the question resolves

verification.name: blocked-not-defaulted
verification.method: the discovery record blocks with the named CRITICAL question and the first attempt leaves the checkout clean

verification.name: answer-durable
verification.method: the operator's answer exists as a durable control_commands row of kind answer

verification.name: value-matches-answer
verification.method: the landed RETRY_LIMIT constant equals the operator's answered value

tasks.title: Schema constant cited from the neighbor contract at its exact OID
tasks.expected_outcome: the plan's citation resolves to lab/neighbor-contracts at the pinned OID and path (validate_plan_citations over the real neighbor git repo); the writable-repo edit implements the cited contract value; the neighbor stays read-only (clean status, unchanged head)
non_goals: no writes to the neighbor repository
no hard-coding values the contract does not state

verification.name: citations-resolve
verification.method: every plan citation resolves to repository + OID + path in the neighbor (the kit's citation validator)

verification.name: neighbor-read-only
verification.method: git status of the neighbor is clean and its head is unchanged after the run

verification.name: value-from-contract
verification.method: the landed constant equals the value read from the cited neighbor file at the cited OID

tasks.title: Rate-limit decision discovered from the neighbor's changelog event
tasks.expected_outcome: the decisive event (the limit change) exists only in the neighbor's CHANGELOG; the plan records and cites it at the exact OID, the edit lands the cited limit in src/limits.py, and the neighbor remains read-only
non_goals: no writes to the neighbor repository
no limit value may come from anywhere but the cited changelog line

verification.name: citations-resolve
verification.method: the changelog citation resolves to repository + OID + path

verification.name: neighbor-read-only
verification.method: git status of the neighbor is clean and its head is unchanged after the run

verification.name: limit-matches-changelog
verification.method: the landed limit equals the value in the cited changelog line

tasks.title: Operator steer reaches the running lane over the durable control plane
tasks.expected_outcome: the operator's guidance is a durable control_commands row (kind steer) recorded before the lane runs; the lane runs with its steering bridge attached over real HTTP and carries a steering journal naming the steer; the deliverable reflects the steered path
non_goals: no acceptance-policy changes (a steer never grants authority)
no human edits to the candidate — the steer is guidance only

verification.name: steer-durable
verification.method: the steer exists as a control_commands row in the control-plane database

verification.name: journal-names-the-steer
verification.method: the lane meta's steering journal holds an entry of kind steer

verification.name: steered-path-landed
verification.method: the candidate carries the steered artifact (the guidance's named file)

tasks.title: Operator pause checkpoints the WIP; the resume completes the turn
tasks.expected_outcome: the pause is a durable command with a verified checkpoint uploaded over real HTTP; the resume command re-admits the work; the resumed lane completes and the final candidate carries BOTH the pre-pause and post-resume edits (AT-01 seam outcome)
non_goals: no fresh restart of the paused work (the resume must restore the exact WIP)
no edits after the collector ran

verification.name: checkpoint-verified
verification.method: the pause's capture receipt is verified and its artifact id is recorded

verification.name: resume-restored-exact-wip
verification.method: the resumed workspace-generation pointer names the checkpoint id and the restored pre-pause bytes are present in the candidate

verification.name: both-legs-in-diff
verification.method: the collected diff carries the pre-pause edit AND the resumed-turn edit

tasks.title: Runner lost before any useful work: the retry dispatches fresh
tasks.expected_outcome: the bootstrap death is journaled on the run row; the authenticated /retry through the real service produces exactly one new native dispatch whose recorded inputs carry lane_resume_mode=fresh with no checkpoint prerequisite (AT-02 seam outcome, asserted on the native server's dispatch ledger)
non_goals: no checkpoint may be demanded (no useful work existed)
no lane subprocess runs in this task (the death precedes the vendor)

verification.name: ledger-carries-fresh-retry
verification.method: the native server's dispatch ledger holds exactly two dispatches for the run and the last inputs carry lane_resume_mode=fresh

verification.name: decision-evidence-bound
verification.method: the run's continuation evidence names mode fresh and no_checkpoint_baseline true

verification.name: client-stayed-on-modeled-surface
verification.method: the native server's unknown_paths list is empty

tasks.title: Revoked checkpoint blob halts loudly; the operator retry recovers fresh
tasks.expected_outcome: the rotted referenced blob makes the required-continuation lane halt wip_restore_failed with ZERO vendor events after the pause leg and zero publication (AT-03 seam outcome); the operator's fresh retry then completes the task with the same intended edit
non_goals: no silent fresh restart may replace the failed required resume
no vendor turn may run against the rotted authority

verification.name: halt-was-loud
verification.method: the first resumed lane exits non-zero with wip_restore_failed and a failed candidate.meta.json

verification.name: zero-vendor-events-after-pause
verification.method: the vendor event log holds no events after the pre-pause leg

verification.name: fresh-retry-completed
verification.method: the retry attempt's collector reports a non-empty generation diff with the intended edit

tasks.title: Cross-runner continuation restores the exact WIP into a new generation
tasks.expected_outcome: the first runner's WIP is checkpointed over real HTTP; a SECOND runner (fresh checkout, fresh lane subprocess, required resume) restores the exact bytes into a new workspace generation and completes its own turn; the shipped collector captures changed, new AND deleted files; both checkouts survive intact (AT-01 seam outcome)
non_goals: the first runner's checkout must never be mutated by the resume
no human edits — the candidate is exactly restored-WIP plus the resumed turn

verification.name: restored-bytes-in-candidate
verification.method: the collected diff carries the pre-checkpoint edit's exact bytes

verification.name: generation-pointer-names-checkpoint
verification.method: the resumed checkout's workspace-generation pointer names the checkpoint id

verification.name: both-checkouts-intact
verification.method: the first checkout still holds its WIP bytes and the resumed checkout is clean at its base
